description.en: Comfort when you're home, savings at price peaks

hint.en: Normal, High (over High above: a warning) or Expensive (over Expensive above: no heating).
Set the tub's own filter cycles here: the start times for the next day, once its prices are known. Cycle 1 always runs; disable cycle 2 when it doesn't run.
Turn the heater on here, for example set its own heater mode or thermostat to the target temperature.
Turn the heater back to rest here.
The ready time ended, or heating ready was turned off by hand.
A ready time started, or heating ready was turned on by hand.
Use it to run other actions when the zone enters or leaves eco, for example an air conditioner's own fan mode.
Runs once a day at the check time set in the Home Controller settings, when tomorrow's prices are still missing or partial.
Without a power meter (a wood-burning stove): the temperature has stopped rising, or is falling, during a session.
Once per session, at the first löyly: the humidity jumps once the sauna is warm.
A session started: the stove draws power, or (without a meter) the temperature rises.
Once per session, when the stove's thermostat first switches off or the ready temperature is reached. Not when someone is already bathing.

title.en: Heating held by the price ceiling

hint.en: Runs once when the hot water runs low (below Keep) while the price is over the home's ceiling (Home Controller: Expensive above), so nothing heats until the price drops. Water temperature: the top of a tank.

Runs once per ready time, when the start of heating for it is known, at most a day ahead. A Hot Tub tells its main heating, after any pre-heating in cheap hours. A Water Heater with Plan from: when the prices for the night are known, with its night block (write Start and Minutes into a schedule in the heater, so it heats also when Homey is down). Otherwise the plan may still change with prices.

title.en: Heating started for a ready time

hint.en: Runs once per ready time, when the main heating for it starts, also after Heating ready was turned on by hand. Not for pre-heating in cheap hours, nor when heating again after the water was ready.
Runs once per ready time, when the water first reaches the target temperature for it.
Runs once when a ready time is not heated for because heating for it would cost more than the price limit.
E.g. guests in a guest room. Running it again adds 24 hours. Afterwards the zone returns to its Occupancy setting.
Ends Away: zones follow occupancy and prices again.
Ends Follow home now.
Everyone is away for days. Starts Away now: zones go to eco and stop cooling until the end of the given day.
Home: someone is home. Coming home: someone is on the way home. Out: nobody is home right now. Use any presence source you like, such as presence or a geofence. For days away, use Away.
Auto, manual or off. Boost is separate: use Boost zone.

title.en: Turn heating ready on or off

hint.en: Off ends the ready time now. On heats to the target temperature now and holds it until turned off, at most as long as set in the device settings.
Turns boost on: heat to comfort plus the boost amount (cooling: comfort), then back to normal. Also sets the zone mode to Auto. Empty time: the boost time from the zone settings.
For a stove whose main switch is seen by another device, e.g. an input on its supply. Once set, the switch starts and ends the session.
For a tank's temperature at one height from a flow, e.g. MQTT. Choose From a flow for that height when adding the device or in Repair.
The temperature when someone is home. Not below eco heat: eco follows if needed.
Only for zones with an air conditioner.
The temperature when nobody is home or the price is expensive. Not above comfort heat: comfort follows if needed.
Only for zones with an air conditioner. Not below comfort cool: comfort follows if needed.
For a water temperature from a flow, e.g. MQTT. Choose From a flow as the water temperature when adding the device or in Repair.
A one-off ready time: the next time it is this time of day. 0 minutes = as long as in the settings.

titleFormatted.en: Ready at [[time]], [[ahead]] minutes ahead, on Mon [[mon]], Tue [[tue]], Wed [[wed]], Thu [[thu]], Fri [[fri]], Sat [[sat]], Sun [[sun]]

hint.en: The Ready at time, how many minutes before it the water is ready, and the days of the week.
The next ready time is not heated for.
Currency shown with the prices, for example € or kr.

When the price counts as expensive. Rate is highest: short local price peaks (needs 15-minute prices; with hourly prices Above average is used). Above average: see the Above average group. Off: occupancy alone decides.
High level for the whole home, 0 for none. Above it Price level is High: a warning for flows, heating runs as planned.

Expensive level for the whole home, 0 for none. Above it the price is always expensive, whatever the model: Price level is Expensive, zones follow their peak rule, and hot tubs and water heaters don't heat at all (not even to hold Keep), except a water heater's night block.
Both models: a price must be at least this much above the median or average to count as expensive, so cheap and flat days are not flagged.
Local time (HH:mm) of the daily check. The trigger Prices missing for tomorrow runs when tomorrow's prices are still missing or partial.
An expensive quarter is more than this above today's average.
Last day away as YYYY-MM-DD. Setting a day turns Away on; it ends after that day. Empty: no end date.
Hourly outdoor temperature for the next days from open-meteo.com, for the Homey's location rounded to about 1 km. Off: the current outdoor temperature counts.
Optional: ready when the sauna sensor reaches this. 0 = when the stove's thermostat first switches off (with a power meter), or the learned temperature.
Left on alarm when a session lasts longer.
The sauna sensor's temperature when the stove's thermostat first switches off.
From switching on to ready, per hour.
Hard limit: heating demand always stops here.
HH:mm, empty for none. One-offs and skips come from flows.
Ready this long before the ready time.
Kept at the target temperature this long.
Ready reached this close to the ready time is held to the end of Keep ready for. Reached earlier, the plan may let it cool and heat again in cheaper hours.
Heating ready turned on by hand or by a flow is held until turned off, at most this long.
Power while heating. With a power meter, the power while heating and the base load (such as a circulation pump) are learned.

The tub's own filter cycles, which also heat. Planned in the cheapest quarters of their windows once the next day's prices are known; the Filter cycles planned card gives the start times to your flow.
HH:mm. The cycle runs in the cheapest quarters between from and to, within one day.
The same length as set on the tub's own filter cycle card.
HH:mm. The cycle runs in the cheapest quarters between from and to, within one day.
The same length as set on the tub's own filter cycle card.
Skip the cycle on a day when its cheapest time costs more per kWh on average. 0 = always runs.
The last planned filter cycles.
Learned where the tub's own heater stops during a filter cycle (needs a power meter). The heating plan counts this heat; until it is seen, filter cycles count as adding none.
Heats just in time until the curve is learned, then also ahead in cheap hours.
Share of the difference to the surroundings lost per hour.
How much higher the water temperature reads while the water stands still. Planned with the reading minus this.
Learned from the power meter: heating, and the base load such as a circulation pump. Above halfway between them counts as heating.
Below this the tank is heated to its target temperature, whatever the price. With tank sensors it is the top temperature (the hot water at the tap). Also keeps the water hot enough while away.
Hard limit: heating demand always stops here.
Used when no room temperature sensor was chosen.
HH:mm, empty for none. One-offs and skips come from flows.
Ready this long before the ready time.
Kept at the target temperature this long.
Ready reached this close to the ready time is held to the end of Keep ready for. Reached earlier, the plan may let it cool and heat again in cheaper hours.
Heating ready turned on by hand or by a flow is held until turned off, at most this long.
Skip a ready time when heating for it, or the ready time itself, would cost more per kWh. 0 = always heat. Keep is always held.

HH:mm, empty for none. The night heat-up: the cheapest Longest block from this time to the next ready time, planned when its prices are known and told by Heating planned (for the heater's own schedule). Outside it only cheaper top-ups and Keep. Empty: the price plan alone.
The night block's length, e.g. the heater's own timer: enough to heat a cold tank. Heating that stops well before it is the thermostat: the tank is at its target temperature.
Power while heating. With a power meter, the power while heating and the base load (such as a circulation pump) are learned.
Heats just in time until the curve is learned, then also ahead in cheap hours.
Share of the difference to the surroundings lost per hour.
How much higher the water temperature reads while the water stands still. Planned with the reading minus this.
Learned from the power meter: heating, and the base load such as a circulation pump. Above halfway between them counts as heating.
Learned with a power meter: where the tank's own thermostat stops the heater. Ready times and reheats heat to it.
Keep heating in the cooling and off seasons, e.g. a bathroom floor.
Follows home: comfort when someone is home or coming home. Always eco: e.g. a guest room. Always comfort: ignores who is home.
Stays at eco and goes to comfort only while the zone is colder than comfort, e.g. a ceiling heater next to a heat pump. Best with a room sensor.
Zone problem alarm when the zone temperature falls below this, in every mode. The app does not heat for it. 0: no alarm.
Boost heats to comfort plus this. When cooling, boost uses comfort.
How long boost lasts when started from the device or without a time.
How long a linked door or window may be open before the zone goes to eco. 0: at once.
Eco: the eco setpoint. Off: the zone's devices are switched off. Ignore: prices do not change this zone.
Over Expensive above (Home Controller). As at price peaks: the setting above applies. Allow comfort: the zone stays at comfort (e.g. an A/C), unless the price model finds a peak too.
Uses the outdoor temperature set on the Home Controller.
In between, heating stays as it was.
Devices, roles and per-device options (thermostat step, relay controls and band, inverted relay, air conditioner eco and between-seasons mode) are changed with Repair, not here.

label.en: Relay minimum on and off time

hint.en: Protects relays and heaters from rapid switching.

Home: someone is home. Coming home: someone is on the way home. Out: nobody is home right now. Set it from your own presence source with the Set occupancy card. Home and Coming home aim at comfort, Out at eco.
The price now against the home's levels: High above (a warning, heating as planned) and Expensive above (zones to eco, hot tubs and water heaters don't heat).
Heating: the stove is on. Ready: hot (the stove's thermostat switched off, or the ready temperature). In use: someone threw the first löyly. Off: no session.

Pre-heating: heating ahead of a ready time in cheap hours. Heating: heating demand is on otherwise. Ready: at the target temperature for a ready time. Waiting: nothing to heat yet. Stopped: no water temperature, or at Maximum. Off: the mode is Off.
Auto: the app sets the members. Manual: hands off, you control the members. Off: the members are off. Boost is a separate switch.
On while the water is held at the target temperature. Turn on to use it now: heats now whatever the price. Turn off to end it.
The zone aims at its eco setpoint (eco heat, or eco cool when cooling).
The current price is expensive by the chosen price model.
Everyone is away for days: zones at eco and no cooling. Off: home.
Hours left that the zone follows who is home instead of its Occupancy setting. 0: off.
When it is expected at the temperature it heats to, by the learned heating: Now when it is there, – when nothing is planned.
When heating starts next: a time, Now while heating, or – when nothing is planned.
Prices are known up to this local time.
Why the app made its latest decision.
While heating: how long until the water reaches the temperature it heats to, by the learned heating curve.
